summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable and Studio did not run (simulation status skipped; simulation_allowed false). The scenario is the Cool-3D baseline Splash2 fft steady-state run on a 3-layer stack (4 cores, 2 MB shared L2, 32 memory banks, passive heat sink). The paper's printed layer maxima are 395.52 K (core layer), 392.83 K (middle memory layer) and 390.57 K (top memory layer). The proposed experiment kind is custom_2d_steady, but it has no floorplan blocks and no power_w, so the input gate fails (a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object). Since it is a steady run, there is no transient trace. No bundled EV6/GCC adaptation and no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace2.5D inputs were used, so no source commit or generated-placement assumption applies, and no illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace was produced. Because the gate is closed, comparison_valid is false and no numerical comparison to 395.52 K, 392.83 K or 390.57 K is made. Qualitatively, the paper attributes the core0 hotspot to higher instruction counts (about 5.87x the other cores on average) and shows the core layer hotter than the memory layers. This cannot be checked against any Studio output. The mismatches are: (1) the paper is a 3D stack with vertical inter-layer coupling, while Studio is 2D/2.5D; (2) block geometry and per-block power are not published; (3) HotSpot 7.0 package, material and heat-sink parameters are not published, and the power model (gem5/McPAT/CACTI-3DD) differs from Studio's; (4) the baseline is passive-cooled, unlike the paper's microfluidic cases; (5) no transient or controller data exist. No exact replication is claimed.

Block geometry and power are missing. The paper gives no block x, y, width or height in metres and no per-block watts for the baseline fft scenario. Fig. 9 shows only a temperature heat map with block labels and a colourbar, so no complete floorplan and power table can be built without inventing values. No pinned assets were supplied (assets list is empty) and the GitHub repository is described as still being released.

The scenario is a 3-layer core-plus-memory 3D stack with a passive heat sink. A 2.5D chiplet placement on an interposer (RLPlanner Ascend910 or ATPlace2.5D) cannot reproduce it, so 3D inter-layer coupling and vertical heat flow are mismatched.

Cooling mismatch. The baseline uses a passive heat sink with no microfluidic cooling, but the paper's main contribution is microfluidic cooling with vertical and 90-degree bent channel patterns in case studies 2a/2b. The baseline observable does not represent those cases.

Solver and power-model mismatch. The paper's power comes from gem5 + McPAT + CACTI-3DD, with per-benchmark and per-unit microarchitectural activity, and temperatures from HotSpot 7.0. A Studio solver with its own package and materials will not reproduce 395.52 K. The paper does not publish the HotSpot material, package or heat-sink parameters needed for calibration.

No optimizer, controller, transient behaviour or reliability analysis is in the baseline scenario. The run is steady-state only, and the paper has no power time series, so transient or controller comparison is not possible.
